summary.conclusion: The learned policy is compared with a domain heuristic, not just a weak retry baseline. This small known environment does not establish that RL is preferable to a deterministic workflow.

algorithm.name: tabular Q-learning
algorithm.epsilon: 0.8 linearly decays to0.04 by85% of training

limitations: Synthetic deterministic sandbox with three tool stages and five known failure categories; no LLM or real service is called.

Fault types and remaining budget are observable; future faults and delays are hidden. Tabular Q values use observations rather than a complete hidden environment state. This is not a language-agent benchmark.
Evaluation holds out exact parameterized fault sequences, not new fault categories. Training uses weighted fault draws; evaluation uniformly samples the held-out finite scenario pool.
Permanent-failure scenarios cannot be completed; safe aborts do not count as task successes.
Q-learning aggregates three checkpoints over identical evaluation scenarios; other baselines run once per scenario. Compare rates, not raw unsafe-action totals.
Training curves include exploration and are not held-out learning curves; the evaluation split is used only after training.
Unsafe attempts are rejected inside the sandbox. Zero attempts in this experiment is not a safety guarantee.
